
## Event Bus System

- To avoid circular dependencies, the event bus is used for certain lifecycle events and business logic events.
- All events are documented, but ownership decides where: engine-published events go in `docs/events.md`; a game module's own events (published by its own code, e.g. `id1`, `hellwave`) go in that module's own `docs/events.md` (`source/game/<mod>/docs/events.md`), linked from `docs/events.md`'s "Game Events" section rather than duplicated into it. This drifts easily since nothing mechanically enforces it — see the `.claude/skills/event-bus-docs-sync/SKILL.md` skill, which is the active trigger to check the right `docs/events.md` whenever an event changes.
- The game code can subscribe to engine events and vice versa.
- The engine can forcefully unsubscribe all listeners from the game when unloading it (e.g. `ClientEngineAPI.eventBus`/`ServerEngineAPI.eventBus` get wiped on every disconnect/map load, since they're per-connection buses) -- `unsubscribeAll()` has no exceptions, by design, so the bus is always genuinely clean when the game stops. Existing game code (`Q1HUD`, `Sync`, `GameManager`, ...) relies entirely on this: listeners are freely (re-)subscribed in per-connection `init()` with no matching individual unsubscribe, so removing the wipe would leak every prior connection's listeners forever.
- `ClientEngineAPI.moduleEventBus` is a second, client-only bus that lives for the whole game module's lifetime instead of being wiped per connection -- for the rare listener that must survive past a single connection (e.g. the menu system's `host.alert`/`host.quit-requested` handlers, which need to keep working even for a connection that's rejected before ever finishing). It carries the exact same event set as `engineAPI.eventBus` (see `clientGameEvents` in `ClientState.ts`) -- the two buses only ever differ in whether *your own* subscription gets wiped on disconnect, not in which events reach them. Subscribe here instead of `engineAPI.eventBus` only when the subscription is set up once (e.g. in `Init()`) and genuinely needs to keep working across reconnects; per-connection listeners should keep using `engineAPI.eventBus` as before. No server-side equivalent exists -- the server isn't reactive the same way (it starts fresh per map load), so there's no "module lifetime" distinct from "map lifetime" worth having.
- Event bus will also allow communication between workers.
